title: The classic 80s vampire film is now a musical- but how does it work o...
transcript: Here's what you can expect when you go to see the Lost Boys musical on Broadway. I am not joking when I say I have gotten more DMs asking me for my thoughts about this show than I have about any other show I have seen. And to be honest, I've been hesitant to make this video because this show is still in early previews. I think I saw the third or fourth preview, and it's one that I very much expect to make a ton of changes over the course of their preview process. In fact, I've heard that since I've seen it, they've already cut at least one song. Now, I do have tickets to go back to the show once it is frozen, meaning they are done making changes. And I will give you my full deep dive thoughts then. But for now, I'm just gonna give you a high level overview of what you can expect from this adaptation. Now, the show is much longer than the movie. The movie is only about 90 minutes, and it's a very quintessential 80s action movie. Thin characters, thin plot, mostly vibes. And so with this additional run time, they're able to add a little bit of depth that wasn't really there in the movie. There's more time to dedicate to the central romance, and they've also developed to the backstory as to how the family ended up in Santa Carla in the first place. They have cut one Major character from the film, that being the grandfather, who in the musical has died before the events of the show. And while he was a very fun character in the film, I do ultimately think cutting him for the musical was the right choice. I actually think on whole, all of the adaptational choices that they've made were really smart. And while it definitely felt a little bit long when I saw it, I know they are actively working too shorten the run time. So hopefully that's something that is resolved over the course of previews. The music itself I found to be a bit of a mixed bag. I think the best songs in the show are the ones sung by the Lost Boys themselves, who in this version of the story, are not just a gang of vampires, but also a rock band. However, a lot of the other songs felt like they could be cut entirely with very minimal impact to the plot or characters. And of course, the main thing people are gonna talk about when it comes to the show, it is visually stunning. The sets, the costumes, the lighting, it is all top notch. The Palace is a very tall theatre, and I felt like they used the height of the stage very well. And the effects are also really cool, including, yes, a lot of flying. But I was a little bit let down by the final sequence of the show. Which again, I won't spoil, but I hope over the course of previews they are able to just beef it up a little bit and give it the narrative weight that it deserves. This is a show with really good bones, but if you can only go once, I would say maybe wait a couple weeks, wait for them to fine tune the things that they need to fine tune, and hopefully the final product lives up to that potential.
reasoning: The reviewer acknowledges good elements (smart adaptational choices, visual spectacle, good Lost Boys songs) but has significant reservations about pacing, some songs feeling unnecessary, and a disappointing finale. The explicit recommendation to 'wait a couple weeks' rather than see it now indicates mixed feelings.
